question: Does the R-512 minimal closed form preserve every scalar normal contraction on its entire form domain, and does its existing spectral semigroup preserve one, after auditing the nonlinear Cauchy shortcut in R-530?

exact_scope.H: R-510 real gauge-invariant state-L2 completion on its original probability state
exact_scope.D: R-511 bounded gauge-invariant globally amplitude-l1-Lipschitz finite-prefix cylinders
exact_scope.form: E(f,g)=(1/2) sum_r nu[c_r Delta_r f Delta_r g], with R-511 inherited conventions
exact_scope.closure: Exactly R-512 form-norm completion V and its injective continuous inclusion into H
exact_scope.scope: K=2, M_s=1, epsilon=1/2, beta=nu=1, m2=theta=0, other OMC-016 couplings one; original two-row strips, labelled all-Q state and j-before-anchored-n construction are inherited; this proof takes no new regulator limit
exact_scope.time: Existing external stochastic Markov parameter t>=0

conclusion.theorem: On the entire R-512 minimal domain V, every scalar normal contraction eta preserves V and satisfies Ebar(eta(u))<=Ebar(u). The same spectral semigroup is positive, L-infinity contractive and preserves one.
conclusion.proof_repair: R-530's direct inference from single-vector contraction to form-Cauchy images is not justified by that estimate. The purported paired-energy and form-distance contraction estimates are false. Replace only that inference by the closed-energy-epigraph argument or the independent weak-compactness/Mazur argument.

exact_negative.scope: Universal paired inequality only; not a PAH carrier or a counterexample to continuity of contractions on form-Cauchy sequences.

conclusion.audit_correction: Supersedes only R-530 certificate section Domain and closure passage and the corresponding inference behind EXP-001649; historical bytes remain unchanged.
